problem: Changing `q[0] <= cutoff` to `q[0] < cutoff` moves the window from (now - window, now] to [now - window, now], so at exactly t + window `allow` refuses and `remaining` returns 0 while `retry_after` (line 49) returns 0.0, telling clients to retry immediately into a refusal.

`setdefault(key, __import__("collections").deque())` does a dynamic import and builds a throwaway deque on every call even for existing keys, leaving the line-2 `deque` import unused (ruff F401) and roughly doubling hot-path cost.
The comment documenting the half-open window contract was deleted and the repository has no tests, so nothing pins the boundary behavior of `allow`/`remaining`/`retry_after` at exactly t + window.
Pre-existing: `_observe` stores `now` without validating it, so a NaN (or non-numeric) timestamp permanently disables the time-went-backwards check or breaks every later call.
Pre-existing: float rounding in `q[0] + self.window - now` can return a wait slightly too short, so a caller who waits exactly `retry_after` is still refused.
Pre-existing: `_accepted` never drops keys and read-only calls insert entries, so client-controlled keys grow memory without bound.
